subject: Request: purchase order mandate variance for SparkLogic pilot
messages:
From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@sparklogic.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Alvarez <marcus.alvarez@sparklogic.io>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot engagement – PO requirement / SOW attached

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re ready to start a 6-week pilot (SparkLogic <> Redwood) but our procurement team needs clarity on your PO mandate. Their standard workflow requires a PO for any engagement, but our internal policy limits issuing a PO until we have an executed SOW and signed vendor terms.

To move quickly we can do the following:
- Start the pilot under a signed SOW and a simple purchase memo (no PO issued for pilots under $12k)
- Or issue a short-term PO and follow up with a full contract after pilot closeout

We’d like to request a temporary variance to your PO requirement so we can begin the pilot on Monday. Attached is the SOW (SOW_SparkLogic_v1.pdf) and a short purchase term summary.

What documentation would you need from us to qualify for a waiver?

Best,
Emily Cho
Head of Partnerships | SparkLogic
emily.cho@sparklogic.io
+1 415-555-0117

Attachments: SOW_SparkLogic_v1.pdf (PDF, 72KB); Purchase_Term_Summary.docx (DOCX, 18KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@sparklogic.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot engagement – PO requirement / SOW attached

Hi Emily — thanks for the SOW and the clear options.

Short answer: our standard policy does require a PO for purchases, but Procurement can approve a temporary variance for pilot engagements under certain controls. To evaluate, we need the following from SparkLogic:
1) Business justification (pilot objectives + expected ARR motion if successful)
2) Total not-to-exceed pilot value (confirm number)
3) W-9 and proof of business address
4) Named point of contact who can sign the SOW

If the pilot is under $15k and you can provide the items above, Procurement may approve a 90-day variance that allows us to start without a PO. Finance will require an acceptance checklist and an assigned GL code for spend tracking.

Looping in Ben and Priya to confirm the finance/procurement constraints and any additional controls. If we can get an internal approval today, I can send a short approval note to your team and provide a DocuSign envelope for the SOW.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

- We can allow a temporary no-PO start for pilots up to $12,500 with the controls Marissa listed. Anything above that threshold needs a PO or a CFO approval.
- Required from vendor before we start: completed W-9 (US entities), invoice remit details, and the SOW signed by an authorized rep.
- Please confirm GL code when you open the pilot so we can track spend.

If Procurement wants to lift the threshold to $15k we’ll need a one-time written approval from my manager. Otherwise we stick to $12.5k.

Team — forwarding with a short recommendation.

Recommendation: Approve a 60-day variance (no PO required) for pilots <= $12.5k with these controls:
- Vendor W-9 and SOW signed and uploaded to vendor record
- Invoice routed to Finance with GL code: 500-ENG-SW (or project-specific code)
- Variance expires automatically after 60 days unless procurement issues a PO
- Product/AE must confirm success criteria in writing and provide a handoff to Customer Success for renewal discussions

If Ben can confirm he’s comfortable with $12.5k, I’ll mark the vendor allowlist entry and issue the temporary variance in the portal. If Ben wants $15k, we need one-level escalation to his manager.

Priya Natarajan
Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference

Emily — good news. Procurement has approved a temporary variance so SparkLogic can start the pilot without a PO under the following conditions:

1) Pilot value must not exceed $12,500 (not-to-exceed).
2) SparkLogic provides: signed SOW (DocuSign link below), completed W-9, and invoice remit info before start.
3) Variance duration: 60 days from approval; if pilot continues past 60 days we’ll require a PO.
4) Finance will require the GL code at invoice time (please use 500-ENG-SW unless Marissa confirms a different project code).

Please complete the DocuSign signing and return the W-9 to procurement@redwood.ai. I’ve attached the SOW to the thread for reference and included a DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/sparklogic/Envelope12345

Next steps for SparkLogic:
- Sign SOW via DocuSign (link above)
- Upload W-9 to the envelope or email to procurement@redwood.ai
- Confirm pilot start date and point of contact

We’ll countersign and confirm variance activation once paperwork is in. Looking forward to getting you started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
